neighbours.label: ' fact' in the emphatic hedge 'in fact' (and similar assertive emphasis like 'indeed')
fire: The plan sounded risky, but in fact it saved the company a great deal of money.
Many people assume bats are blind; in fact, most species see quite well.
She said she was tired, and in fact she fell asleep before the film started.
Critics called the bridge unsafe, though in fact it passed every inspection.
The old map was thought to be lost, but it was in fact sitting in the archive.
He claimed he had never met her, when in fact they had worked together for years.
The drug was expected to fail, and yet it did in fact reduce the symptoms.
Some think the desert is lifeless; it is in fact full of small animals.
quiet: The plan sounded risky, and it cost the company a great deal of money.
Many people assume bats are blind, and some species do see poorly.
She said she was tired, so she went to bed before the film started.
Critics called the bridge unsafe, so it was closed for a full inspection.
The old map was thought to be lost, so they searched the whole archive.
He claimed he had never met her, and nobody in the office argued.
The drug was expected to fail, and the trial was stopped after a month.
Some think the desert is lifeless because it gets so little rain.

notes: Card is broad (1.3%); top peaks ' fact' x6, ' that', ' indeed'. Near misses keep 'fact' or emphasis-free phrasing without the hedge.
